chapters.summary: Epstein introduces Introduction 685 by the Speaker, which would establish an Office of Insurance Accountability to address rising insurance costs that impact every New Yorker and every city agency.
chapters.title: Chair Epstein outlines Intro 685 establishing Office of Insurance Accountability

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: Today we're voting on legislation aimed at combating the rise of cost of insurance in New York.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: It impacts every New Yorker and every single agency.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: It's introduction 685 by the Speaker establishing the Office of Insurance Accountability.

chapters.summary: Epstein describes Resolution 387 by Council Member Brewer, calling on the state legislature to pass and the governor to sign A07828A/S07939 and A9015/A9016 to mitigate the rising cost of insurance for affordable housing.
chapters.title: Chair Epstein outlines Res 387 on affordable housing insurance relief

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: Resolution 387 by Councilmember Brewer.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: Which we'll be hearing from soon, calling on the New York State Legislature to pass, the governor to sign A07828A and Senate 07939 and A9015 and A9016.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: to mitigate the cost of insurance.

chapters.summary: Epstein introduces Resolution 389 by Council Member Dinowitz calling for passage of the Automobile Insurance Consumer Information Act (S.1196/A.3893), and Resolution 395 by Council Member Morano calling on the state to prohibit homeowners insurance rate increases exceeding 25% per year.
chapters.title: Chair Epstein outlines Res 389 on auto insurance transparency and Res 395 on homeowners insurance rate caps

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: Resolution by Councilmember Dinowitz, calling on New York State Legislature to pass the governor's sign, the Automobile Insurance Consumer Protection Act.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: Resolution 395 by Councilmember Morano, calling on the state legislature and the governor's sign, S6356 and A4188, prohibiting the increase in rates of homeowner insurance in excess of 5%.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: 25 percentage points a year.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: I would also like to bring over to the sponsors of the resolutions, starting with Councilmember Brewer.

chapters.summary: Brewer explains that insurance for affordable housing is a major challenge to making term sheets work, describes a proposed state relief fund program to provide grants for commercial insurance expenses, and mentions a task force to address the affordable housing insurance crisis and improve availability and pricing.
chapters.title: Council Member Brewer presents Res 387 on affordable housing insurance crisis

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Chair.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: I think you have made it very clear that insurance, particularly for affordable housing, is incredibly challenging.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: I know that many people have tried to address this, and I can't say it's been successful.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: So to the credit of those in Albany, they are trying to create a fund.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: It would be a fund for affordable housing insurance.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: It would be a relief fund program to provide grants.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: To eligible projects for reasonable and necessary commercial insurance expenses.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Right now, as you know, if you build affordable housing, insurance is one of your biggest challenges to making the term sheets work.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Also part of this legislation will be a task force.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: To address the affordable housing insurance crisis and to improve availability and pricing.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: All of this is very challenging, but I think we have to give it our best efforts, and I look forward to...

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: hopefully some positive outcomes.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

chapters.summary: Epstein thanks Brewer and turns the floor to Council Member Dinowitz, who expresses appreciation for the opportunity to speak and notes his enthusiasm for participating in the committee hearing.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: We're so happy to have you here.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: I'm happy to be here.

chapters.summary: Dinowitz notes that auto insurance is mandatory in New York yet no office exclusively represents consumer interests before the Department of Financial Services. He highlights that New Yorkers face an average annual premium of $4,223, nearly twice the national average, at a time when rates have skyrocketed nationally.
chapters.title: Council Member Dinowitz on lack of consumer representation in auto insurance rate setting

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: As we all know, the auto industry, auto insurance is mandatory in New York.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: There's no office or official that exclusively represents consumer interests to the New York State Department of Financial Services.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: This means that at a time when insurance rates have skyrocketed nationally, there is no body analyzing insurers'proposed rate hikes through the lens of consumer advocacy.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: This shortcoming proves especially dire as New Yorkers face an average annual premium of $4,223, which is nearly twice the national average.

chapters.summary: Dinowitz explains that DFS does not publish premium information, disempowering consumers from comparison shopping or assessing the fairness of increases. He describes how Resolution 389 calls on the state to pass S.1196, requiring DFS to publish automobile insurance premium and complaint data on its website to enable consumers to compare plans.
chapters.title: Council Member Dinowitz on Res 389 requiring DFS to publish auto insurance premium data

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: Moreover, DFS does not publish information on insurance premiums, depriving consumers of much-needed transparency when selecting a plan.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: New Yorkers are disempowered, unable to comparison shop or assess the fairness of increase in their coverage.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: And that is why we are passing Resolution 389, which calls on the state to pass Senate Bill 1196, also known as the Automobile Consumer Information Act.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: This bill would require DFS to publish automobile insurance premium and complaint information on its website.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: Enabling consumers to compare plans, and encouraging consumers to buy more.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: Petition based both on cost and quality of coverage.

chapters.summary: Dinowitz details how the bill would establish an Office of Insurance Consumer Advocate to represent consumers before DFS with the ability to request hearings on rate increases. He adds that municipalities could petition for rate reductions and insurers would be required to justify proposed increases in a standardized format for more effective public oversight.
chapters.title: Council Member Dinowitz on Office of Insurance Consumer Advocate and rate oversight provisions

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: It would also establish an Office of Insurance Consumer Advocate to represent consumers'interests before DFS with the ability to request hearings surrounding rate increases.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: Furthermore, municipalities could petition for rate reductions and insurers would be required to justify proposed increases and follow a standardized format in rate applications, allowing for more effective public oversight.

chapters.summary: Dinowitz argues that as the city faces an affordability crisis, car insurance has become far too burdensome for the average working New Yorker and it is the Council's responsibility to act. He thanks his colleagues for their vote on the resolution.
chapters.title: Council Member Dinowitz concludes on affordability crisis and car insurance burden

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: As our city faces an affordability crisis, it's essential that we act to help reduce costs of necessities wherever we can.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: Car insurance has become far too burdensome on the average working New Yorker, and it's our responsibility to take action.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: And I thank my colleagues for their vote on this resolution today.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: Thank you, Chair.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: Thank you, Councilmember Dinowitz.

summary: The Committee on Consumer and Worker Protection, chaired by Harvey Epstein, voted on four insurance-related items: Intro 685 establishing an Office of Insurance Accountability, Res 387 on affordable housing insurance relief, Res 389 on auto insurance transparency, and Res 395 capping homeowners insurance rate increases at 25% per year.

Council Members Gale Brewer and Eric Dinowitz presented their respective resolutions, with Brewer detailing a state-level affordable housing insurance relief fund and Dinowitz advocating for DFS to publish auto insurance premium data and establish an Office of Insurance Consumer Advocate.
All items passed by a roll call vote of 9-0 with no abstentions, and the committee was adjourned.
title: Committee on Consumer and Worker Protection
topic: Establishing an office of insurance affordability
